greek: Καὶ εἶπεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Νωε Εἴσελθε σὺ καὶ πᾶς ὁ οἶκός σου εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, ὅτι σὲ εἶδον δίκαιον ἐναντίον μου ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ.
hint: Noah is told to go in with all his house, the word Hebrews 11:7 uses of the ark's purpose.

notes.text: οἶκος is first *a house, abode, dwelling*, then *household goods, substance*, then *household, family*. Hebrews 11:7 says Noah built the κιβωτός εἰς σωτηρίαν τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ.
δίκαιος, *observant of custom and social rule*, as at 6:9.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH* alone; the Greek adds ὁ θεός.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: ἔτι γὰρ ἡμερῶν ἑπτὰ ἐγὼ ἐπάγω ὑετὸν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τεσσαράκοντα ἡμέρας καὶ τεσσαράκοντα νύκτας καὶ ἐξαλείψω πᾶσαν τὴν ἐξανάστασιν, ἣν ἐποίησα, ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς.
hint: The Hebrew's 'every living substance' is a Greek word Paul uses for resurrection.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *kol-hayqûm*, *all that stands, every living substance*, from *qûm*, *to rise, stand*. The Greek renders the root: ἐξανάστασις, *a rising up from*, which Middle Liddell glosses *resurrection* and knows only from Philippians 3:11, εἰς τὴν ἐξανάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν. At 7:23 the same Hebrew word is ἀνάστημα. Codex Alexandrinus reads πᾶν τὸ ἀνάστημα here too, as Rahlfs's apparatus records.
ἐξαλείφω's first sense is *to plaster* or *wash over*, used of walls; *to wipe out, obliterate* is its second. The Hebrew *ʾemḥeh* is *I will wipe out*, as at 6:7, where the Greek had ἀπαλείφω.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾānōkî mamṭîr*, *I am causing it to rain*. The Greek has *I bring rain*, with ἐπάγω, the verb of the deluge at 6:17.
νύξ is, in Middle Liddell's words, *night*, either *the night-season* or *a night*; the first tagged translation is *the night-season*.

hint: The Greek dates the flood to the twenty-seventh day of the month; the Hebrew, the seventeenth.

notes.text: *On the seventh and twentieth of the month*. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕšibʿâ-ʿāśār yôm laḥōdeš*, *on the seventeenth day of the month*. εἰκάς is *the twentieth day of the month*, one sense, and ἑξακοσιοστός, *six hundredth*, is LSJ's, citing this verse; both are plain text.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *maʿyĕnôt tĕhôm rabbâ*, *the springs of the great deep*; the Greek has no *great*. ἄβυσσος is the word of 1:2.

[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾărubbōt haššāmayim*, *the windows of the heavens*, in the plural. καταρράκτης as a noun is *broken water, a waterfall*, then *a portcullis*, then *a gull*, the bird that rushes down.
Both passive: ῥήγνυμι, *to break*, and ἀνοίγνυμι, *to open*, in that voice. The entry's own passive glosses, *to burst* and *to stand open*, follow in the chains.

greek: καὶ ἐξήλειψεν πᾶν τὸ ἀνάστημα, ὃ ἦν ἐπὶ προσώπου πάσης τῆς γῆς, ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπου ἕως κτήνους καὶ ἑρπετῶν καὶ τῶν πετεινῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἐξηλείφθησαν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς· καὶ κατελείφθη μόνος Νωε καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ κιβωτῷ.
hint: The Hebrew word of 7:4 returns, and the Greek gives it a second word.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *kol-hayqûm* again, which the Greek rendered ἐξανάστασις at 7:4. ἀνάστημα is not in Middle Liddell; LSJ's first sense is *height*, then *protuberance*, *high ground*, *building*.
ἐξαλείφω, *to plaster*, as at 7:4, in the passive.
The Hebrew is *wayyiššāʾer ʾak-nōaḥ*, *only Noah was left*.

greek: καὶ ὑψώθη τὸ ὕδωρ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἡμέρας ἑκατὸν πεντήκοντα.
hint: A hundred and fifty days, as in the Hebrew.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyigbĕrû*, *prevailed*, as at 7:18–20; the Greek has *was lifted high*.
